opencode.label: OpenCode
opencode.description: An open-source AI coding assistant that works with many AI providers (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and local models). It includes a plugin system and built-in multi-agent orchestration for tackling complex tasks.
opencode.use_cases: Good choice if you want flexibility in which AI model to use, prefer open-source tools, or want to keep costs down with OpenRouter. Also great if you plan to use plugins to extend its capabilities.
opencode.auth_hint: Log in via 'opencode auth' on first launch, or set OPENCODE_API_KEY / OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your environment. Your login is preserved between sessions.

claude.label: Claude Code
claude.description: Anthropic's official coding assistant powered by Claude. It works directly in the terminal and can read files, write code, run commands, search your project, and manage git — all through natural conversation.
claude.use_cases: Ideal for complex refactoring, working with large codebases, and security-conscious projects. Excels at understanding existing code and making well-reasoned changes across many files.
claude.auth_hint: Log in via 'claude login' on first launch. Your session is preserved between container restarts. Alternatively, set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your environment.
dockerfile: || ( CLAUDE="$(find /root/.claude /root/.local -name claude -type f 2>/dev/null | head -1)" && [ -n "$CLAUDE" ] && ln -sf "$CLAUDE" /usr/local/bin/claude ) || true

cursor.label: Cursor CLI
cursor.description: The terminal version of Cursor's AI editor. Same AI capabilities as the Cursor desktop app, but running in a command line. It can edit multiple files, run background tasks, and integrate with your existing Cursor subscription.
cursor.use_cases: Best if you already use Cursor's desktop editor and want the same AI in a container. Useful for automated coding tasks and CI/CD pipelines.
cursor.auth_hint: Log in via 'agent auth' on first launch. Your Cursor subscription carries over. Alternatively, set CURSOR_API_KEY in your environment.

copilot.label: GitHub Copilot
copilot.description: GitHub's AI coding assistant running as a command-line tool. It connects directly to your GitHub account and can work with issues, pull requests, and your repository's context.
copilot.use_cases: Best if your workflow centers on GitHub — turning issues into code, automating PR reviews, and working within GitHub's ecosystem. Requires a GitHub Copilot subscription.
copilot.auth_hint: Log in via 'gh auth login' on first launch. Your GitHub credentials are preserved between sessions.
